title: Which alloy composition,what process parameters? Inferring the recipe from optimized metallic microstructure and texture
authors: Mahish K. Guru, Jan Bohlen, Louam Lemjid, Marius Tacke, Roland Aydin, Noomane Ben Khalifa
abstract: The mechanical properties of a metallic alloy are set by its microstructure and texture: the size and shape of its grains and the orientation of their crystals. That structure is in turn set by a recipe, the alloy composition together with the processing parameters. Alloy development runs this chain forwards, tuning the structure until a target property is met. Running it backwards, from an optimized structure to the recipe that would produce it, still relies on expert knowledge. We ask whether this backwards step can be learned. On an in-house dataset of 107 magnesium alloy extrusion conditions across 14 alloys, each with optical micrographs and an X-ray texture measurement, we compare three descriptors of microstructure and texture: conventional grain and texture statistics, a vision embedding from a pretrained image encoder, and a graph neural network on the grain network. Each is paired with prediction heads for two tasks: the alloy composition given the process (Task A), and the process parameters given the composition (Task B). Under 5-fold cross-validation, the conventional descriptors identify the correct alloy for 65% of held-out conditions, against 17% for always guessing the most common alloy, while the learned embeddings stay below 30%. The process parameters are recoverable but noisier: compared with using the composition alone, the microstructure roughly halves the temperature error. Because only a few alloys were cast and only a few press settings were used, both answers are discrete, and heads that pick from these known options, while respecting their order, worked better than heads that predict a free value.

infographic.key_insight: A metallic alloy’s composition and processing recipe can be inferred in reverse from its optimized microstructure and texture, with conventional hand-crafted descriptors outperforming learned embeddings in this small dataset.
infographic.engineering_relevance: This suggests a data-driven route for alloy recipe back-calculation, helping materials engineers narrow candidate compositions and extrusion settings when designing for target properties.
method: Built a 107-sample magnesium alloy extrusion dataset spanning 14 alloys, with optical micrographs and X-ray texture measurements.
Compared three microstructure/texture representations: conventional grain and texture statistics, pretrained vision embeddings, and a graph neural network over the grain network.
Used prediction heads for two inverse-design tasks: infer alloy composition from processing conditions, and infer process parameters from composition.
infographic.evidence_signal: Under 5-fold cross-validation, conventional descriptors identified the correct alloy for 65% of held-out cases versus a 17% majority-class baseline, and they also reduced process-temperature error relative to using composition alone.
infographic.watch_item: The study is limited by a small, discrete dataset with only a few alloys and press settings, so the inverse predictions may not generalize well beyond the observed options.
infographic.paper_title: Which alloy composition,what process parameters? Inferring the recipe from optimized metallic microstructure and texture

title: Accelerating dynamic polarizability calculations of organic molecules using equivariant graph neural networks
authors: Houssam Metni, Maria Kraus, Marie Louise Schubert, Marjan Krstic, Carsten Rockstuhl, Pascal Friederich
abstract: Predicting the dynamic polarizability tensor of organic molecules is essential for simulating light-matter interactions in optoelectronic devices, yet conventional quantum-chemical methods such as time-dependent density functional theory (TD-DFT) are computationally expensive and limit large-scale screening. We present an equivariant graph neural network architecture that predicts frequency-dependent, complex-valued dynamic polarizability tensors directly from readily available molecular information, such as 3D geometry and UV-vis spectra. The model learns to approximate the shape and magnitude of the dynamic polarizability tensor, capturing both dispersive and absorptive features that define the molecular optical response. We evaluate the model on molecules from both the QM9 dataset and the Harvard organic photovoltaic dataset using various metrics, including the earth mover's distance, which is suitable for comparing spectral quantities. For both datasets, the model successfully reproduces the main features of the dynamic polarizability tensor and generalizes across diverse molecules. To assess the applicability, we further validated the model using a downstream workflow to calculate the optical properties of organic photovoltaic devices. We used the model-predicted polarizabilities to perform device-level optical simulations, yielding charge carrier generation rates in agreement with TD-DFT-based results ($R^2 = 0.94$). Our approach offers a promising complement, or even an alternative, to conventional methods such as TD-DFT, enabling faster and more efficient screening of photoactive organic molecules for optoelectronic applications.

infographic.key_insight: An equivariant graph neural network can predict frequency-dependent complex dynamic polarizability tensors of organic molecules from molecular structure, closely matching TD-DFT features at a fraction of the cost.
infographic.engineering_relevance: This enables faster screening of photoactive molecules and device-level optical simulation for organic optoelectronics without relying entirely on expensive quantum-chemical calculations.
method: Uses an equivariant GNN to learn tensor-valued, frequency-dependent polarizability from 3D geometry and UV-vis spectra.
Predicts both dispersive and absorptive components of the complex dynamic polarizability tensor.
Evaluated on QM9 and Harvard organic photovoltaic molecules, then integrated into a downstream device simulation workflow.
infographic.evidence_signal: Across QM9 and Harvard OPV datasets, the model reproduced main spectral features and achieved strong agreement in device-level charge carrier generation rates with TD-DFT-based simulations ($R^2 = 0.94$).
infographic.watch_item: Performance may depend on the availability and quality of molecular geometries, spectra, and representative training data for out-of-distribution chemistry.
infographic.paper_title: Accelerating dynamic polarizability calculations of organic molecules using equivariant graph neural networks

title: Bottom-Up Prediction of Amorphous Poly(1,3-dioxolane) using Ab Initio Reactive Machine-Learning Force Fields
authors: Yizhi Song, Bharatha K. Gunawardana, Kriti Alam, Teresa Shah, Deepa Ranabhat, Hsin-Yu Ko
abstract: Poly(1,3-dioxolane) (pDXL) is a chemically recyclable polyether that can be synthesized by living cationic ring-opening polymerization with precise control of chain length into the ultra-high-molecular-weight (UHMW) regime, where it acquires enhanced mechanical properties. Like most polymers, however, it has amorphous condensed-phase structure, and diffraction measurements alone cannot resolve the atomistic microstructure that underlies them. In this work, we predict the ensemble of the pDXL microstructures by applying a recently developed AI-accelerated ab initio bottom-up polymer structure prediction (AI$^{2}$-BPSP) framework that simulates the living polymerization of pDXL under experimental synthetic conditions with machine-learning force fields trained within van der Waals-corrected hybrid density functional theory. Partitioning the predicted X-ray and neutron diffraction signal between the growing chain and the surrounding monomer resolves its dominant feature into two counteracting modes: a monomer contribution near $q \approx 1.5$ Å$^{-1}$ that decays as monomer is consumed, and a polymer contribution near $q \approx 1.6$ Å$^{-1}$ that is absent in oligomers and grows with chain length. This work paves the way to direct accuracy validation of these statistically significant, first-principles, and chain-length resolved diffraction predictions against experiments.

infographic.key_insight: AI2-BPSP predicts the atomistic microstructure and diffraction signature of amorphous poly(1,3-dioxolane) by simulating its living polymerization from first principles.
infographic.engineering_relevance: This enables structure-guided design and validation of ultra-high-molecular-weight recyclable polymers whose mechanical performance depends on amorphous chain packing that experiments alone cannot fully resolve.
method: Simulated living cationic ring-opening polymerization under experimental synthetic conditions.
Used machine-learning force fields trained on van der Waals-corrected hybrid DFT.
Partitioned X-ray and neutron diffraction into monomer and growing-polymer contributions across chain lengths.
infographic.evidence_signal: The predicted diffraction feature at q ≈ 1.5–1.6 Å⁻1 separates into a monomer peak that decays with monomer consumption and a polymer peak that grows with chain length.
infographic.watch_item: The predictions are statistically and computationally intensive, and direct experimental validation is still needed for the chain-length-resolved diffraction assignments.
infographic.paper_title: Bottom-Up Prediction of Amorphous Poly(1,3-dioxolane) using Ab Initio Reactive Machine-Learning Force Fields

title: Deep learning driven framework for optimization of polycrystalline microstructures under competing strength requirements
authors: Ashwini Gupta, Indrashish Saha, Lori Graham-Brady, Tamer A. Zaki
abstract: Computational design of polycrystalline microstructures for enhanced mechanical performance requires repeated high-fidelity simulations over stochastic morphologies, rendering conventional crystal plasticity finite element (CPFE) approaches prohibitively expensive for optimization. Here, we develop a deep learning-driven framework for optimizing polycrystalline microstructures under competing quasi-static and dynamic performance requirements. A 3D U-Net surrogate maps polycrystalline copper microstructures directly to full-field velocity histories from plate-impact simulations, preserving the spatial and temporal resolution needed to evaluate dynamic performance and interrogate underlying wave interactions and failure mechanisms. The surrogate is coupled with stochastic microstructure generation and derivative-free optimization to efficiently navigate the design space. To monitor surrogate reliability during optimization, we introduce a distribution-consistent reliability region (DCRR) based on maximum mean discrepancy (MMD) to quantify distributional shift from the training data. The framework is demonstrated for multiple design problems, including constrained optimization of spall and yield strengths and inverse design. The optimal designs are validated using CPFE simulations with less than 3% prediction error across all optimization cases, while the surrogate-driven optimization reduces cumulative evaluation time by approximately four orders of magnitude compared with direct CPFE-based optimization. Although demonstrated here for the design of polycrystalline microstructures targeting spall and yield strengths, the framework is broadly applicable to optimization problems where high-fidelity full-field simulations are prohibitively expensive but spatially and temporally resolved response information is essential for evaluating, interpreting, and optimizing candidate designs.

infographic.key_insight: A deep learning surrogate can directly predict full-field microstructure response, enabling fast optimization of polycrystalline copper for competing spall and yield strength targets.
infographic.engineering_relevance: The framework makes expensive CPFE-based microstructure design practical by preserving the spatial and temporal detail needed for performance assessment while cutting optimization cost by orders of magnitude.
method: 3D U-Net maps 3D polycrystalline microstructures to velocity histories from plate-impact simulations.
Stochastic microstructure generation plus derivative-free optimization searches the design space.
DCRR using MMD monitors distribution shift to flag surrogate reliability during optimization.
infographic.evidence_signal: Validated optimal designs matched CPFE results with less than 3% prediction error, and surrogate-driven optimization reduced cumulative evaluation time by about four orders of magnitude.
infographic.watch_item: Reliability depends on staying near the training-data distribution, so extrapolation beyond the DCRR region may weaken surrogate accuracy.
infographic.paper_title: Deep learning driven framework for optimization of polycrystalline microstructures under competing strength requirements

title: Grain-boundary segregation delays the onset of plastic flow in nanocrystalline Fe-18Cr-12Ni
authors: Ashwinee Kumar
abstract: Grain-boundary (GB) segregation in austenitic Fe-Cr-Ni alloys has been studied mainly in irradiated or sensitised material, rarely in the nanocrystalline state. Hybrid molecular dynamics/Monte Carlo (MD/MC) simulations are used to segregate three independent nanocrystalline Fe-18Cr-12Ni polycrystals, which are compared with annealed and random controls on the same microstructures. Ni is depleted at the GB plane and Cr is enriched in the adjacent atomic shell; both directions are established at the production sampling budget and strengthen when one of the three microstructures is sampled further. The Cr enrichment is resolved only against the far-field grain interior; the common partition into face-centred-cubic (fcc) and non-fcc atoms places the enriched shell in its own reference. Under a constant uniaxial stress of 4.6 GPa at 300 K, the segregated polycrystals take about 16% longer than random ones to reach 50% strain; measured against annealed controls, boundary chemistry contributes about two-thirds of this gain and boundary relaxation the rest. The difference arises from a lower strain rate early in plastic flow, with no resolvable change in dislocation content. At a fixed strain rate the segregated state has a 6-7% higher peak stress than its annealed control at 300, 750 and 950 K, and at matched ratios of applied to flow stress the gain is the same at all three temperatures, decreasing only as that ratio rises. Early plastic flow is thus the stage at which GB chemistry acts, and simulated GB composition in nanocrystals depends strongly on the reference region.

infographic.key_insight: Grain-boundary segregation in nanocrystalline Fe-18Cr-12Ni delays the onset of plastic flow by slowing early deformation, with Cr-enriched and Ni-depleted boundaries strengthening the alloy response.
infographic.engineering_relevance: Targeting grain-boundary chemistry offers a practical route to improve high-temperature strength and delay yielding in nanocrystalline stainless steels.
method: Hybrid molecular dynamics/Monte Carlo simulations on three independent nanocrystalline Fe-18Cr-12Ni polycrystals
Comparison against annealed and random controls on the same microstructures
Constant-stress and fixed-strain-rate mechanical tests across multiple temperatures
infographic.evidence_signal: Under 4.6 GPa at 300 K, segregated polycrystals reached 50% strain about 16% later than random ones, and showed a 6-7% higher peak stress than annealed controls at 300, 750, and 950 K.
infographic.watch_item: The measured segregation strength depends strongly on the chosen reference region, so composition metrics must be interpreted carefully when comparing studies.
infographic.paper_title: Grain-boundary segregation delays the onset of plastic flow in nanocrystalline Fe-18Cr-12Ni

title: Small Distortions, Big Polarization: Tetragonal BaTiO3 Nanoparticles for High-Performance Piezoelectric Nanogenerators
authors: Shivshankar Jokare, Vikash Kushwaha, Mandar Shirolkar, Shruti Kharadkar, R. Boomishankar, Smita Chaturvedi
abstract: Lead-free ferroelectric BaTiO3 (BTO) nanoparticles with stabilized tetragonal distortion were synthesized via a ligand-assisted sol-gel method to serve as the active piezoelectric phase in high-performance hybrid piezoelectric nanogenerators (PENGs) operating with triboelectric synergy. XRD, Raman spectroscopy, and Pair Distribution Function (PDF) analysis confirmed pseudo-cubic tetragonal BTO nanoparticle, annealed at 900°C (BTO-900, ~54nm) and well-defined tetragonal BTO annealed at 1200°C (BTO-1200, ~104nm). Density Functional Theory (DFT) calculations confirmed enhanced Ti-O covalency, stronger Ti 3d-O 2p hybridization, narrower HOMO-LUMO gap, and improved dipole coherence in BTO-900, indicating superior ferroelectric polarization, piezoelectric activity, and charge retention. BTO-900-PDMS PENG device generated a high open-circuit voltage of ~100 V and stored ~29 μJ energy, and superior capacitor-charging performance of BTO-900, while the optimized BTO-1200 based device showed a higher power density of ~649 μW cm-2 and short-circuit current of ~181 μA. The superior performance of BTO-900 was attributed to enhanced defect-assisted charge trapping, interfacial polarization, and impedance-controlled charge retention. By coupling the intrinsic piezoelectric response of covalency-engineered tetragonal BTO with triboelectric charge generation at the BTO-PDMS interface, this work establishes nanoparticle size and bonding engineering as an effective route to high-output, lead-free piezoelectric nanogenerators for self-powered electronics.

infographic.key_insight: A small tetragonal distortion in BaTiO3 nanoparticles, stabilized by size and bonding control, can markedly boost ferroelectric polarization and piezoelectric output in lead-free nanogenerators.
infographic.engineering_relevance: This work shows that tuning nanoparticle crystallography and interface chemistry can improve self-powered device performance for wearable and low-power electronics.
method: Ligand-assisted sol-gel synthesis of BaTiO3 nanoparticles
Structural/chemical verification with XRD, Raman, and PDF analysis
DFT to probe Ti-O covalency, band gap, and dipole coherence
infographic.evidence_signal: The abstract reports ~100 V open-circuit voltage and ~29 µJ energy storage for BTO-900, while BTO-1200 reached ~649 µW cm-2 power density and ~181 µA short-circuit current.
infographic.watch_item: Performance depends on nanoparticle size, tetragonal distortion, and interfacial charge trapping, so device optimization may not transfer directly across processing conditions or packaging formats.
infographic.paper_title: Small Distortions, Big Polarization: Tetragonal BaTiO3 Nanoparticles for High-Performance Piezoelectric Nanogenerators

title: Automatically Building and Updating a Knowledge Graph of MLIP Models
authors: Alexis Beer, Liudmyla Klochko, Mathieu d'Aquin
abstract: Complementing the many efforts in providing semantic representations of concepts, notions, and entities in materials science, we report and illustrate a process by which we can automatically build a knowledge graph of the fast evolving field of machine learning applied to the prediction of material properties, focusing on MLIP (Machine Learning Interatomic Potential). This LLM-based process relies on multiple steps, from information extraction in documents and articles to a validation loop using SHACL constraints to detect and correct errors. It is carried out on a model-by-model basis, focusing on the consistency of representation, therefore enabling an iterative construction where the addition of new models is facilitated. We illustrate the process by showing a few interesting aspects that can be queried from a knowledge graph built from the models listed in the Matbench Discovery leaderboard.

infographic.key_insight: The paper presents an automated, LLM-assisted pipeline to build and continuously update a knowledge graph for ML interatomic potential (MLIP) models, enabling consistent representation of a rapidly changing research landscape.
infographic.engineering_relevance: This approach helps materials engineers and data curators organize, compare, and query MLIP models more reliably, supporting faster discovery and more maintainable model registries.
method: Extract model information from documents and articles using LLM-based information extraction.
Validate and correct entries with SHACL constraints in an iterative error-detection loop.
Build the graph on a model-by-model basis to preserve consistency and simplify future updates.
infographic.evidence_signal: The abstract reports that the process was demonstrated on models listed in the Matbench Discovery leaderboard, showing that the resulting knowledge graph can support useful queries over real benchmarked MLIP models.
infographic.watch_item: Because the pipeline depends on automated extraction and constraint-based correction, ontology coverage and SHACL rule design may strongly affect completeness and error rates.
infographic.paper_title: Automatically Building and Updating a Knowledge Graph of MLIP Models

title: PoreML: A Data-Driven Framework for Learning Multiphase Flow in Porous Media
authors: Chunyang Wang, Mingrui Zhang, Yuyan Zhang, Linqi Zhu, Xin Ju, Edo Sicco Boek
abstract: Multiphase flow in porous microstructures is central to CO$_2$ storage, fuel-cell operation, and flip-chip packaging. Predicting these flows remains challenging because wettability and complex pore geometry govern the nonlinear evolution of fluid interfaces. Machine learning holds substantial promise for advancing the field, but progress is constrained by scarce time-resolved 3D datasets and a lack of a unified workflow for training and evaluating models. To fill this critical gap, we introduce PoreML, an open-source framework unifying data generation, model training, and evaluation grounded in pore-scale physics. The framework comprises three core components. (a) A modern GPU-native lattice Boltzmann solver, validated against analytical solutions and published experiments, enables reproducible data generation. (b) A 3.3 TB dataset contains 560 simulation runs and 158,546 stored time steps across four application-driven scenarios. These trajectories span synthetic structures and geometries derived from micro-CT scans of real materials, covering diverse wetting conditions and viscosity ratios. (c) A unified learning framework evaluates one-step prediction and autoregressive rollouts. Its domain-specific evaluation protocols assess predictive accuracy and physical consistency. We evaluate five models of diverse architecture under these protocols. Two complementary challenges assess transfer to larger domains and from synthetic to micro-CT-derived structures. PoreML provides a shared foundation for machine-learning research on multiphase flow in porous media, with the aim of empowering the community to develop reliable predictive models and advance the field.

infographic.key_insight: PoreML provides an end-to-end, pore-scale machine-learning workflow for learning and evaluating multiphase flow in porous media from large, physics-grounded simulation data.
infographic.engineering_relevance: It can accelerate design and screening for technologies where fluid displacement in complex pores matters, such as CO2 storage, fuel cells, and packaging.
method: GPU-native lattice Boltzmann solver for reproducible data generation
3.3 TB dataset with 560 runs and 158,546 time steps across synthetic and micro-CT-derived geometries
Unified training and evaluation for one-step prediction and autoregressive rollouts with physics-aware protocols
infographic.evidence_signal: The abstract reports five model architectures tested under unified protocols, plus two transfer challenges targeting larger domains and synthetic-to-micro-CT generalization.
infographic.watch_item: Performance may still be limited by domain shift between synthetic and real porous structures, especially when extrapolating to larger or less well-characterized geometries.
infographic.paper_title: PoreML: A Data-Driven Framework for Learning Multiphase Flow in Porous Media

title: Progress and Prospect of AI in ARPES Workflow
authors: Sandy Adhitia Ekahana, Aalok Tiwari, Pratik Saud, Aaron Bostwick, Chris Jozwiak, Eli Rotenberg
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is becoming an increasingly useful tool across the experimental sciences, including angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES), which routinely produces large, multidimensional datasets of electronic structure. Recent advances in AI and machine learning (ML) have opened new opportunities across the entire ARPES workflow, from automated sample preparation and real-time data acquisition to post-experiment data analysis and comparison with theoretical calculations. Despite this progress, a comprehensive review of ML applications, their capabilities, and reliability across the different stages of ARPES workflow is still lacking. In this review, we first introduce ML methods that are most relevant to experimentalists working in condensed matter physics and materials science. We then follow the ARPES workflow, reviewing existing ML applications at each step and discussing their advantages, limitations and potential for future development. We also examine the current ARPES data landscape, where several open databases are available but remain relatively small and fragmented compared with large, shared datasets such as ImageNet. Given these limitations, we suggest that the community focus on sharing pretrained models that can be further trained, adapted to specific tasks, and redistributed, while working toward a larger and standardized open ARPES dataset repository. Finally, we discuss our perspectives on the future of AI within the ARPES workflow using a six-level framework of laboratory automation, highlighting the opportunities and challenges in moving toward a fully autonomous, self-driving ARPES laboratory.

infographic.key_insight: AI/ML can support nearly every stage of the ARPES workflow, from sample prep and data collection to analysis and theory comparison, but adoption depends on better shared datasets and reliable pretrained models.
infographic.engineering_relevance: For computational materials workflows, the paper highlights a path toward more automated, scalable, and reproducible ARPES experiments using AI-driven acquisition and analysis tools.
method: Surveyed ML methods relevant to condensed matter experimentalists
Mapped AI applications across the full ARPES workflow
Discussed a six-level framework for laboratory automation and self-driving ARPES
infographic.evidence_signal: The review notes that ARPES has multiple open databases, but they are still small and fragmented compared with large benchmark datasets like ImageNet.
infographic.watch_item: A major limitation is the lack of standardized, large-scale ARPES datasets, which can restrict model reliability, transferability, and validation.
infographic.paper_title: Progress and Prospect of AI in ARPES Workflow

title: Origins of Universal Machine Learning Force-Field Errors in Multicomponent Materials
authors: Hongwei Du, Dingyang Lv, Baole Wei, Yu Ren, Feng Yu, Xin He
abstract: Universal machine learning force-field generalization to multicomponent environments generated by compositional design remains insufficiently assessed. We construct a benchmark of 7,599 multicomponent configurations inspired by high-entropy design, elemental substitution and anion mixing. Eleven pretrained models are evaluated against density functional theory for energies, forces and stresses, with assessment extended to elastic, vibrational and adsorption-related properties. Force errors are analysed through training-reference coverage, local geometric heterogeneity, distance directionality and elemental response. Distances to training-reference environments reveal a qualitative association between coverage differences and increasing errors, while substantial variation remains at similar distances. Higher-error groups show greater local geometric heterogeneity, although OMat24 provides broad coverage of these environments. Relative to training-reference pair medians, errors remain low near the median, rise steeply on the compression side and increase more weakly on the extension side. After matching element pairs and absolute distance deviations, compression-side force errors are 1.81-1.95 times extension-side errors. Model-predicted pairwise interaction curves show greater curvature under compression. Fitting difficulty in independent elemental systems correlates with electronic band-energy responses to atomic displacements and Fermi-level shifts, and a similar pattern is observed in multicomponent systems. In parameter-matched comparisons, spherical-harmonic representations with maximum degrees of 2 and 4 lower test force errors for 38 and 40 of 43 elements, respectively, while differences in elemental difficulty remain. These findings inform force-field selection for experimental compositional design and identify targets for training-data sampling and model representations.

infographic.key_insight: Universal machine-learning force fields make larger errors in multicomponent materials when local environments are underrepresented, highly heterogeneous, or compression-dominated.
infographic.engineering_relevance: For compositional design workflows, model choice and training-data coverage should be matched to the target chemistry and strain state to reduce force-field failure risk.
method: Built a benchmark of 7,599 multicomponent configurations inspired by high-entropy design, elemental substitution, and anion mixing.
Evaluated 11 pretrained models against DFT for energies, forces, stresses, and downstream elastic, vibrational, and adsorption-related properties.
Analyzed error drivers using training-reference distance, local geometry, directionality of interatomic separation, and elemental response patterns.
infographic.evidence_signal: Across the benchmark, force errors generally increased with distance from training-like environments, and after matching pair types and distance deviations, compression-side force errors were about 1.81–1.95× larger than extension-side errors.
infographic.watch_item: Coverage metrics help explain trends but do not fully predict error magnitude, so near-identical distances can still yield substantially different failures.
infographic.paper_title: Origins of Universal Machine Learning Force-Field Errors in Multicomponent Materials

title: Electronic Properties of Ladder-Type Phenylenes Studied by Thermally-Assisted-Occupation Density Functional Theory
authors: Tsu-Hsuan Wang, Jeng-Da Chai
abstract: Accurate prediction of the electronic properties of extended $π$-conjugated systems with radical character remains a major theoretical challenge. To overcome this challenge, thermally-assisted-occupation density functional theory (TAO-DFT) has been developed in recent years. In this study, we employ TAO-DFT to systematically explore the electronic properties of ladder-type phenylenes ($n$-LPs), containing $n$ fused four-membered carbon rings. Our calculations reveal that all investigated $n$-LPs (with $n$ = 1 ~ 40) possess singlet ground states. With increasing $n$-LP size, we observe a transition from the nonradical character of smaller $n$-LPs to the polyradical character of larger $n$-LPs. Notably, we identify a distinct damped periodic oscillation in the radical character of $n$-LPs, featuring highly correlated hotspots at specific intervals ($n = 3k - 1$, where $k$ are positive integers). The real-space representation of active orbitals confirms this global electronic behavior is governed by the structural localization of active orbitals along the central ladder framework. These findings provide fundamental insights into the size-dependent electronic properties of $n$-LPs, guiding their rational design for future nanomaterial applications.

infographic.key_insight: TAO-DFT shows that ladder-type phenylenes remain singlets but evolve from nonradical to polyradical behavior as the fused-ring length increases, with a damped periodic hotspot pattern at n = 3k - 1.
infographic.engineering_relevance: These size-dependent electronic trends help guide the rational design of extended π-conjugated nanomaterials with tunable radical character and electronic functionality.
method: Applied thermally-assisted-occupation density functional theory (TAO-DFT) to n-LPs with n = 1–40.
Analyzed ground-state spin character, radicality, and frontier/active orbitals across molecular sizes.
Used real-space active-orbital representations to link electronic behavior to structural localization along the central ladder framework.
infographic.evidence_signal: The study systematically evaluated a size series of 40 ladder-type phenylenes and identified consistent singlet ground states plus an oscillatory radical-character pattern with hotspots at n = 3k - 1.
infographic.watch_item: TAO-DFT predictions are computational and depend on the chosen functional/occupation model, so experimental validation is still needed for larger or more strongly correlated systems.
infographic.paper_title: Electronic Properties of Ladder-Type Phenylenes Studied by Thermally-Assisted-Occupation Density Functional Theory

title: First-Principles Investigation of Multimodal Toxic Gas Sensing in Carbon-Tuned hBN-Graphene Alloys: Chemiresistive, Work-Function, and Optical Responses
authors: Tanjuma Shikder Jhumu, Ahmed Zubair
abstract: Compact, reliable, and cost-effective gas sensors have become a highly demanding subject for safety management in the medical sector, chemical manufacturing, food quality monitoring, agriculture, and industrial safety. Hazardous gas emissions need to be controlled and monitored with fast-responsive and highly sensitive sensing devices. A first-principles study employing density functional theory (DFT) was used to investigate the adsorption behavior of Cl2, CO, CO2, NO, NO2, and HCN gas molecules with our proposed alloys, which consisted of hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) and graphene (Gr). The alloy consisting of 22% carbon (BNGr-2) was found to be most competent for sensing Cl2, CO, CO2, and HCN with sufficient adsorption energy, charge transfer, and bandgap alteration. However, NO and NO2 gas molecules showed more engagement with 33% carbon-proportioned alloy (BNGr-3) in terms of adequate gas sensing properties. NOx gases exhibited the most chemiresistive sensitivity towards the adsorbents. Other gases also showed significant chemiresistive sensitivity and distinct selectivity ratios, which would facilitate these alloys as chemiresistive sensors. Besides, noticeable work function variation (~20%) of these systems manifested potential as work function based sensors. Cl2 and NO2 showed strong physical adsorption, while the rest of the gases were weakly to moderately physisorbed, resulting in very short recovery times (10-1 ~ 10-6 seconds). Additionally, the distinctive absorption spectra observed for the gas analyte systems highlighted the potential of the proposed alloys as optical gas sensors. Temperature variation revealed that all gas molecules can be freed from the adsorbent BNGr-2 at 425 K. These findings imply hBN-Gr alloys as promising gas sensors for pollution auditing.

infographic.key_insight: Carbon-tuned hBN-graphene alloys, especially BNGr-2 and BNGr-3, can sense toxic gases through multiple complementary signals: resistance change, work-function shift, and optical response.
infographic.engineering_relevance: The study suggests a single alloy platform for compact, fast, and selective toxic-gas sensors for environmental monitoring, industrial safety, and pollution auditing.
method: Used first-principles density functional theory (DFT) to simulate gas adsorption on hBN-graphene alloys.
Compared adsorption energy, charge transfer, bandgap change, chemiresistive response, work-function shift, and optical spectra for Cl2, CO, CO2, NO, NO2, and HCN.
Assessed thermal recovery behavior and temperature effects to estimate sensor reusability.
infographic.evidence_signal: The abstract reports strong selectivity and sensitivity trends, including ~20% work-function variation, very short recovery times (10^-1 to 10^-6 s), and complete gas release from BNGr-2 at 425 K.
infographic.watch_item: These are simulation-based results, so experimental fabrication, defect tolerance, and real-world selectivity in humid or mixed-gas environments still need validation.
infographic.paper_title: First-Principles Investigation of Multimodal Toxic Gas Sensing in Carbon-Tuned hBN-Graphene Alloys: Chemiresistive, Work-Function, and Optical Responses

title: Agentic Resource Allocation for Batch Multi-Objective Bayesian Optimization in Autonomous Materials Discovery
authors: Robert Robinson, Shakti Prasad Padhy, Sushant Sinha, Sk Md Ahnaf Akif Alvi, Juan Florez Coronel, Brent Vela
abstract: The discovery and development of advanced materials is a challenging process constrained by the high time and monetary costs of synthesis, processing, and characterization. The underlying design spaces can be enormous, often with multiple competing objectives. Bayesian optimization (BO) provides a principled approach for efficiently navigating such spaces, but most workflows rely on fixed exploration-exploitation policies that lack the capacity to adapt to shifting constraints in dynamic campaigns typical of self-driving laboratories. In this work, we develop a multi-objective BO framework for alloy design under resource constraints, benchmarking strategies for adaptive policy tuning at each iteration. Our evaluation covers a septenary refractory high-entropy alloy (RHEA) system focused on maximizing melting temperature and minimizing density, and an Fe-Co-Ni-based soft magnetic alloy system targeting saturation magnetization, coercivity, and hardness. We compare an exploitation-focused strategy, a fixed mixed exploratory/exploitative policy, and two distinct LLM-based adaptive strategies with different approaches to batch allocation and campaign signal interpretation, evaluated across baseline and mid-campaign resource event conditions including budget reductions, timeline cuts, and combined disruptions. Our results show that mixed allocation strategies accumulate substantially more mutual information than the exploitation-focused baseline at a proportionally smaller cost to hypervolume and optimization speed, with adaptive strategies outperforming a fixed-mixed allocation policy by adjusting their allocation in response to both evolving campaign statistics and resource constraints. These findings suggest that adaptive resource allocation offers a favorable tradeoff for materials discovery campaigns in reducing predictive uncertainty on Pareto-optimal compositions.

infographic.key_insight: Adaptive, resource-aware batch Bayesian optimization can better balance exploration and exploitation in autonomous materials discovery, improving Pareto-front learning under changing campaign constraints.
infographic.engineering_relevance: For self-driving laboratories, the work suggests that dynamically reallocating experiments can reduce uncertainty and preserve discovery efficiency when budgets, timelines, or other resources shift.
method: Compared three allocation policies: exploitation-focused, fixed mixed exploratory/exploitative, and LLM-based adaptive strategies.
Tested multi-objective Bayesian optimization on two materials systems: a septenary refractory high-entropy alloy and an Fe-Co-Ni soft magnetic alloy.
Evaluated performance under baseline and mid-campaign disruptions including budget cuts, timeline reductions, and combined resource events.
infographic.evidence_signal: Across the abstracted benchmarks, mixed and adaptive allocation strategies gained substantially more mutual information than pure exploitation, with adaptive policies improving over fixed-mixed allocation under resource disruptions.
infographic.watch_item: Results are benchmark-based, so real-world gains may depend on the quality of the campaign state signals and the reliability of the LLM-driven allocation decisions.
infographic.paper_title: Agentic Resource Allocation for Batch Multi-Objective Bayesian Optimization in Autonomous Materials Discovery

title: Mechanical properties of V-4Ti-4Cr alloy from molecular dynamics with a neural-network potential
authors: G. S. Demyanov, D. V. Minakov, S. B. Saltykov, P. R. Levashov, N. M. Chtchelkatchev
abstract: Machine-learning interatomic potentials enable large-scale atomistic simulations of vanadium alloys relevant to fusion applications, but reliable training and validation remain challenging in multicomponent systems. Here, we develop a descriptor-based DeepMD-DPA1 potential for the V-Ti-Cr system using a two-stage workflow: broad configuration sampling driven by the MatterSim foundation model followed by fine-tuning to density-functional-theory data computed with VASP. The model achieves root-mean-square errors of 9.2 meV/atom for energies and 0.23 eV/angstrom for force components. Using this potential in large-cell LAMMPS simulations, we compute Young's modulus, bulk modulus, and Poisson's ratio for V-4Ti-xCr and V-xTi-4Cr alloys at T = 300 K and T = 1073 K. We find that increasing Cr fraction increases the elastic moduli of the alloy, while increasing Ti fraction decreases them; all compositions are softer at 1073 K than at 300 K. Two-phase simulations give a melting temperature for pure V of 1950 K, in good agreement with experimental data.

infographic.key_insight: A two-stage DeepMD neural-network potential trained for the V-Ti-Cr system captures elastic behavior of V-4Ti-4Cr alloys and predicts how composition and temperature tune stiffness.
infographic.engineering_relevance: The results support composition-by-design of vanadium alloys for fusion applications by showing that Cr strengthens while Ti softens the alloy, and that high temperature reduces elastic moduli.
method: MatterSim was used to generate broad configuration sampling for the V-Ti-Cr space.
The potential was fine-tuned to VASP density-functional-theory data.
Large-cell LAMMPS simulations were then used to compute elastic constants at 300 K and 1073 K.
infographic.evidence_signal: The reported model accuracy is 9.2 meV/atom for energies and 0.23 eV/angstrom for force components, and it predicts a 1950 K melting temperature for pure V close to experiment.
infographic.watch_item: Accuracy depends on the coverage of the training set, so extrapolation to compositions, defects, or temperatures outside the sampled domain may be unreliable.
infographic.paper_title: Mechanical properties of V-4Ti-4Cr alloy from molecular dynamics with a neural-network potential

title: Reinforcement Learning on the Discrete Composition Channel of a Crystal Generator: Validated Gains and Reward Hacking
authors: Pawan Prakash, Philipp Höllmer, Addis Fuhr, Peter Hirschfeld, P. Ganesh, Stefano Martiniani
abstract: Inverse materials design is a long-standing goal of computational materials discovery. Generative models for crystalline materials are typically trained to match the distribution of a structure database, while nothing in their training objective points them at specific design goals such as targeted properties. We use group-relative policy optimization (GRPO) to align a generative model based on stochastic interpolants and discrete flow matching with general black-box reward functions through reinforcement learning. Atom types are generated by a discrete flow and the policy gradient of our generalization of GRPO directly acts on the likelihoods of the atom-type transitions, which differentiates our work from previous reinforcement-learning approaches for diffusion and flow-based generative models of crystalline materials. We introduce a reward function that raises the yield of metastable, unique and novel structures (mSUN) from 13.4% for the pretrained model to 45.5% for the reinforced model, as evaluated by a community benchmark. Our reward also improves the performance of a reinforcement learning framework for crystalline materials based on latent denoising diffusion models. At the same time, we find that directly reinforcing atom-type transition likelihoods enables reward exploitation that has to be prevented with explicit guards. The same analysis also exposes a gap in the community metric. Single-element structures in distinct packings are counted as metastable, unique and novel materials and inflate mSUN without yielding any new compounds. A stability claim is only as good as its reference hull. We report every result split by the number of reference phases behind it and argue that benchmarks should do the same.

infographic.key_insight: GRPO can directly steer a crystal generator’s discrete atom-type transitions toward desired materials rewards, substantially improving targeted structure yield while revealing reward-hacking risks.
infographic.engineering_relevance: This shows a practical reinforcement-learning route for inverse materials design, enabling black-box optimization of crystal generators for properties beyond imitation of training data.
method: Apply group-relative policy optimization to a stochastic-interpolant / discrete flow-matching crystal generator.
Update policy on discrete atom-type transition likelihoods rather than only latent or continuous denoising variables.
Use explicit safeguards to limit reward exploitation and track performance by reference-hull context.
infographic.evidence_signal: The reinforced model raised metastable, unique, and novel (mSUN) yield from 13.4% to 45.5% on a community benchmark, with additional analysis split by the number of reference phases.
infographic.watch_item: Directly optimizing discrete atom-type transitions can exploit the reward function, so guards and benchmark reporting must prevent inflated scores from trivial single-element packings.
infographic.paper_title: Reinforcement Learning on the Discrete Composition Channel of a Crystal Generator: Validated Gains and Reward Hacking

title: SOTA: Stock Options Trading Agents Guided by Option-Implied Return Distributions
authors: Yizhen Xie, Mengyang Liu
abstract: As option markets grow and AI advances, agentic systems for option trading are gaining increasing attention. Language-model-based agents can reason over contextual information such as news, but option trading presents a particularly challenging decision problem: a single stock can have thousands of contracts, and the agent must decide both which contracts to trade and how to combine them. Existing approaches often sidestep this complexity by restricting the policy to a fixed strategy structure, such as a straddle, limiting their ability to switch strategies as market conditions change. We present SOTA (Stock Options Trading Agents), an agentic trading framework for structured option-strategy selection. SOTA abstracts the large option universe into strategy-level decisions while deterministic resolvers handle portfolio implementation. We develop SOTA by post-training Qwen3.8-27B with supervised fine-tuning followed by reinforcement learning. SOTA is evaluated on options on nine large-cap U.S. equities and SPY against rule-based and machine-learning strategy selectors in the same trading environment. Over a six-month out-of-sample period, SOTA earns an 18.3% total return with a Sharpe ratio of 1.60 and a maximum drawdown of 8.96%. We also document an asymmetric role of news: news improves frontier-teacher trajectories, but retaining news during reinforcement learning reduces out-of-sample return from 18.3% to -2.7%.

infographic.key_insight: SOTA turns option trading into structured strategy selection, using an agent to choose the strategy while deterministic rules build the actual options portfolio.
infographic.engineering_relevance: The framework reduces the complexity of trading thousands of option contracts by making the decision space strategy-level, which is useful for practical AI-assisted portfolio systems.
method: Post-trains Qwen3.8-27B with supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning.
Abstracts the option universe into strategy decisions, with deterministic resolvers executing the final trades.
Uses option-implied return distributions and news context to guide policy learning and action selection.
infographic.evidence_signal: On a six-month out-of-sample test across options on nine large-cap U.S. equities plus SPY, SOTA achieved 18.3% total return, a 1.60 Sharpe ratio, and 8.96% maximum drawdown.
infographic.watch_item: Retaining news during reinforcement learning caused performance to drop sharply out of sample, suggesting sensitivity to information leakage or train-test mismatch in the news pipeline.
infographic.paper_title: SOTA: Stock Options Trading Agents Guided by Option-Implied Return Distributions

title: OxiGen: Oxidation-State-Aware Crystal Generation
authors: Dylan John, Kim E. Jelfs, Alex M. Ganose, Eleonora Giunchiglia
abstract: Generative models have the potential to accelerate inorganic materials discovery by enabling inverse design, but generating experimentally realisable crystals remains challenging. Oxidation states are widely used to assess the compositional validity of crystals and guide inorganic materials discovery. While existing generative models for crystals can generate materials with charge-neutral oxidation-state assignments, they poorly reproduce the distributions of oxidation states observed in synthesised materials. To address this limitation, we propose OxiGen, an oxidation-state-aware crystal diffusion model that explicitly represents oxidation states during generation. OxiGen enforces global charge neutrality by construction using a structured output layer with exact inference over a finite-state automaton. Empirically, OxiGen substantially improves oxidation-state fidelity, generates the highest rate of stable, unique, and novel crystals among evaluated methods, and maintains high compositional validity even under property conditioning.

infographic.key_insight: OxiGen adds explicit oxidation states to crystal diffusion generation, improving chemical realism while enforcing exact charge neutrality.
infographic.engineering_relevance: This makes inverse design for inorganic materials more practical by generating candidate crystals that are more likely to be synthetically and compositionally valid.
method: Oxidation-state-aware crystal diffusion model that represents oxidation states during generation.
Structured output layer with exact inference over a finite-state automaton to guarantee global charge neutrality.
Supports property-conditioned generation while preserving compositional validity.
infographic.evidence_signal: According to the abstract, OxiGen improves oxidation-state fidelity and achieves the highest rate of stable, unique, and novel crystals among evaluated methods, while maintaining high validity under property conditioning.
infographic.watch_item: Exact inference and structured decoding may add implementation complexity and could make scaling or integration with other generative pipelines less straightforward.
infographic.paper_title: OxiGen: Oxidation-State-Aware Crystal Generation

title: Powder-in-tube confinement as a design principle for fatigue-resistant caloric materials
authors: T. Niehoff, L. Beyer, J. Puy, F. Scheibel, J. Freudenberger, O. Gutfleisch
abstract: Caloric solid-state refrigeration offers an energy-efficient alternative to vapor-compression cooling, but many of the most promising materials, including the magneto- and elastocaloric Heusler alloys, are intrinsically brittle and fail under the cyclic loading required in operation. Here, we introduce mechanical confinement via powder-in-tube (PIT) processing as a general strategy to overcome this limitation. By embedding a granular Heusler alloy core of 87 % packing density within a ductile steel sheath (2.8 mm outer diameter, 0.3 mm wall thickness), the composite confines the brittle powder and enables effective load transfer between particles. While the core remains inherently brittle, the surrounding sheath prevents catastrophic fragmentation and turns brittleness from a disqualifying property into a manageable one. We demonstrate that this approach enhances mechanical durability by several orders of magnitude, with the composites sustaining 100,000 load cycles at 250 MPa without structural failure and tolerating overload stresses up to 700 MPa. Confinement also alters the transformation itself, and to resolve this behavior in these mechanically complex systems, we developed a simultaneous in-situ measurement technique combining strain and AC magnetic susceptibility under load. It reveals that the internal stress field in the core is strongly heterogeneous. As a consequence, the macroscopic strain decouples from the transforming phase fraction, and the martensitic transition cannot be tracked by mechanical data alone. Mechanical confinement thus emerges as a design principle for fatigue-resistant caloric materials, and the combined in-situ method as a characterization tool for composite, porous, and other mechanically heterogeneous caloric systems.

infographic.key_insight: Powder-in-tube mechanical confinement turns brittle Heusler caloric powders into fatigue-resistant composites by preventing catastrophic fragmentation and improving load transfer.
infographic.engineering_relevance: This provides a scalable design strategy for durable solid-state cooling materials that can survive the repeated loading required for practical caloric refrigeration.
method: Packed Heusler alloy powder to 87% density inside a ductile steel tube (2.8 mm OD, 0.3 mm wall).
Applied cyclic mechanical loading while measuring strain and AC magnetic susceptibility simultaneously in situ.
Used the combined signals to probe heterogeneous internal stress and transformation behavior under load.
infographic.evidence_signal: The composites survived 100,000 load cycles at 250 MPa without structural failure and withstood overloads up to 700 MPa.
infographic.watch_item: Macroscopic strain alone does not track the martensitic phase fraction in these heterogeneous composites, so interpretation requires coupled mechanical and magnetic measurements.
infographic.paper_title: Powder-in-tube confinement as a design principle for fatigue-resistant caloric materials

title: Defect-limited thermal transport in AlN using pretrained machine-learning interatomic potentials
authors: Minseok Moon, Wonjun Choi, Seungwu Han, Youngho Kang
abstract: Aluminum nitride (AlN) is an important thermal management material whose high lattice thermal conductivity is strongly suppressed by oxygen impurities. We investigate phonon scattering by oxygen-related defects using pretrained universal machine-learning interatomic potentials (MLIPs), molecular dynamics (MD), and phonon Boltzmann transport calculations. Several pretrained MLIPs are benchmarked against density functional theory for phonon dispersions and pristine thermal conductivity. To balance accuracy and computational speed, we use a fine-tuned version of the compact SevenNet-Nano model for MD simulations. Monte Carlo annealing supports the formation of bound $V_{\mathrm{Al}}(\mathrm{O_N})_3$ complexes, whose scattering differs from that of their isolated constituents. Defect scattering rates extracted from excess spectral energy density (SED) linewidths agree reasonably with harmonic $T$-matrix predictions at low oxygen contents, supporting the independent-scatterer approximation. Incorporating these rates into an iterative Boltzmann transport equation with Bose--Einstein statistics yields thermal conductivities comparable to experimental values and captures their observed decrease with oxygen content. At high concentrations, however, the scattering rate deviates from linear scaling with oxygen content, suggesting limitations of independent-defect and pristine-phonon descriptions. These results demonstrate an efficient approach using pretrained MLIPs to quantify defect-limited thermal transport and provide insights into impurity effects beyond the dilute-defect approximation.

infographic.key_insight: Pretrained machine-learning interatomic potentials can efficiently capture how oxygen-related defects suppress thermal transport in AlN, including defect complexes and non-dilute scattering effects.
infographic.engineering_relevance: The approach provides a practical route to predict and tune thermal conductivity in AlN thermal-management materials under realistic impurity conditions.
method: Benchmark several pretrained MLIPs against DFT for phonons and pristine thermal conductivity
Use a fine-tuned SevenNet-Nano model in molecular dynamics and Monte Carlo annealing to form defect complexes
Extract defect scattering from SED linewidths and feed it into iterative BTE calculations
infographic.evidence_signal: The defect scattering rates and thermal conductivities were compared against harmonic T-matrix predictions and experimental trends, with good agreement at low oxygen content and realistic conductivity decrease with increasing oxygen.
infographic.watch_item: At higher defect concentrations, scattering no longer scales linearly with oxygen content, so dilute independent-defect assumptions and pristine-phonon models can break down.
infographic.paper_title: Defect-limited thermal transport in AlN using pretrained machine-learning interatomic potentials

title: Lattice dynamics of disordered phases of silicon and spatially resolved computations of thermal conductivity
authors: A. Gautam, C. Ugwumadu, L. A. M. Rosset, R. M. Tutchton, S. Nakhmanson, D. A. Drabold
abstract: The lattice dynamics of disordered systems (amorphous solids, polymers and glasses) are often distinct from crystalline analogues. Examples include the "two-level systems" and the Boson peak. Here, we show that even the venerable material amorphous silicon offers new wrinkles: (1) realistic networks studied with DFT-quality interatomic potentials show the existence of harmonic modes exhibiting anomalously large root-mean-square variation in atomic positions, and (2) these dynamics determine the processes of heat transport. We correlate the atomic dynamics with transport using the site-projected thermal conductivity [C. Ugwumadu et. al Phys. Status Solidi B 263, e202500316 (2026)], and conjecture that these observations are relevant to other disordered systems.

infographic.key_insight: Disordered silicon hosts harmonic vibrational modes with unusually large atomic displacement fluctuations, and these same local dynamics are tied to how heat flows through the material.
infographic.engineering_relevance: Understanding and mapping site-resolved lattice dynamics in amorphous silicon can guide thermal management and transport modeling in disordered semiconductor and glassy materials.
method: Use DFT-quality interatomic potentials to model realistic amorphous silicon networks.
Analyze harmonic vibrational modes and identify atoms with anomalously large root-mean-square positional variations.
Correlate atomic dynamics with site-projected thermal conductivity to link structure, motion, and heat transport.
infographic.evidence_signal: The abstract reports realistic-network simulations showing anomalously large RMS atomic displacement modes and a spatially resolved thermal-conductivity correlation, though no quantitative metrics are given here.
infographic.watch_item: Because the conclusion is drawn from modeled disordered networks and site-projected analysis, transferability to other materials and sensitivity to model realism should be validated carefully.
infographic.paper_title: Lattice dynamics of disordered phases of silicon and spatially resolved computations of thermal conductivity
